name: starting architecture
last_analysis: No scores are visible, so I have to rely on priors and on what the trials cover. Every trial so far trained without errors. With the default recipe, the policy changes only about 32 times per run (4,096 samples per update). That is very few, and it is probably a stronger limit than the network. Of the networks tried, the stem-skip net (r2c2) is the cheapest refinement: it adds about 8% compute and sends sharp per-column information to the footprint head, which is the most direct route to judging where a brick lands and whether it matches the target. The per-cell head (r3c1) is a natural extension of it. In this last round I keep the networks known to train and change mainly the update schedule: half as many parallel worlds (128), so the policy updates more than twice as often. I also use a longer horizon (gamma 0.97 to 0.99), so the bonus for an exact build reaches back through the whole episode and the agent learns better when to choose DONE.
